openings.how-to-boost-your-hrv: Measure HRV at the same time each morning with the same device, and act on the weekly trend, not the daily score. Sleep timing, alcohol and training load move HRV more than any breathing drill does.
openings.how-to-improve-sleep-quality: A fixed wake time, seven days a week, does more for sleep quality than any supplement or gadget. Everything else in this guide builds on that one habit.
openings.creatine-complete-guide-for-executives: Creatine monohydrate at 3 to 5 grams a day is the best studied supplement in sport. It supports strength training, and the evidence on thinking and memory is early but promising.
openings.how-to-lose-fat-without-losing-performan: You can lose fat and keep your strength if you keep lifting, eat enough protein and cut calories slowly. Crash dieting costs you the muscle you spent years building.
openings.how-to-do-a-chin-up: Most adults can get their first chin up in 8 to 12 weeks with three short sessions a week. The route is dead hangs, then rows, then negatives, then the first rep.
openings.vo2-max-for-executives-longevity-metric: VO2 max is the strongest single fitness predictor of how long you live. Two to three easy aerobic sessions a week plus one hard one will raise it at any age.
openings.founder-guide-stress-management-system: Founders do not need a mindset. They need a review process: workload, sleep, training and recovery looked at together every week.
openings.zone-2-training-busy-professionals: Zone 2 is the pace where you can still speak in full sentences. Two 45 minute sessions a week is enough for most busy professionals to build an aerobic base.
openings.morning-routine-executives-data-not-podc: The best morning routine for an executive is a regular wake time, 10 minutes of outdoor light and a look at last night's sleep data. Nothing else is required.
openings.executive-fitness-program-strength-cardi: After 40, the priority order is strength twice a week, easy cardio three times a week, and sleep protected above both. Supplements come last.
openings.ceo-burnout-recovery-protocol: Burnout is a workload problem before it is a fitness problem. Cut the load first, then rebuild sleep, then training.
openings.olympic-training-principles-business-per: Olympic athletes train in blocks with planned easy weeks. Executives who copy that structure recover better and perform more consistently than those who push every week.
openings.whoop-for-business-performance-data-guid: WHOOP is useful for trends over weeks, not for daily decisions. Use it to catch a slow slide in sleep or recovery, not to decide whether to train today.
openings.alcohol-and-performance-what-data-says: Two drinks in the evening measurably reduce sleep quality and overnight HRV in most people. The effect is dose dependent and clears in one to two nights.
openings.periodisation-for-non-athletes-training-: Periodisation means planning training in phases of 3 to 6 weeks with a lighter week between them. It works for a 50 year old founder as well as it works for an Olympian.

about: Strength and Conditioning Coach, Australian Men's Water Polo Team, October 2021 to present. National Lead S&C through four international campaigns: 2023 World Championships in Fukuoka, 2024 World Championships in Doha, the Paris 2024 Olympic Games, and the 2025 World Championships in Singapore. Now supporting the LA28 pathway.

First worked with the Australian national water polo program in 2015, supporting Rio Olympic preparation across Sydney camps and test series against Japan and Italy. Assistant coach and S&C with the Australian team at the World University Games in Taipei.
Founder, Otion, September 2023 to present. Health and performance coaching for founders, executives and organisations.
TRX Master Instructor, 2008 to 2023. Trigger Point Master Trainer, 2012 to 2021.
Strength and conditioning for Australian Water Polo League clubs: West Magpies, Drummoyne Devils, Balmain Tigers.
Former New Zealand Men's National Water Polo Team athlete. Trained under Hungarian coach Dénes Kemény.
Qualifications: ASCA Level 2 (Australian Strength and Conditioning Association), Certificate IV in Fitness, TRX Master Instructor, Institute of Motion certified.
